topology: 1 node x2 A100 PEs over one ConnectX-5, NVSHMEM put-ring forced through the NIC with P2P disabled, GPU-initiated (IBGDA)
why: the only case that exercises device-initiated networking. Every other IB case captures the CPU's data plane (ibv_post_send/poll_cq); IBGDA has no CPU data plane at all, so this is the one capture that proves the mlx5dv/DEVX provider sees traffic the ibverbs provider structurally cannot.
why_no_goldens: a golden here would pin qp_num, LID, umem_id and dmabuf fd — every one of which is assigned by the fabric or the allocator and varies run to run. That is the failure this suite has been walking back all week (case 01's qp_num 449 collision, case 06's 115-vs-114 regions, case 05's fabricated peers). There is nothing here worth characterizing that is not also allocation-dependent, so this case carries assertions only.
platform_note: MareNostrum 5's ACC partition CANNOT run this: NVSHMEM reports 'no active IB device that supports GPU-initiated communication', nvidia_peermem is not loaded and PeerMappingOverride is unset (jobs 44156334/44156479/44156594). du04 has both, which is why it runs there. job.sbatch pre-flights those prerequisites and reports SKIP rather than failing on a host that cannot do IBGDA — a skip is honest, a red board would not be.
loopback_note: Both PEs sit on one node behind ONE HCA, so src_lid == dest_lid on every connection. That is CORRECT here and an assertion forbidding self-LID edges would be wrong — unlike case 02, where a self-edge was the bug. The invariant that survives loopback is closure: every dest_qp_num must resolve to a queue pair some rank actually created.
workload_note: `mpirun -np 2 ... putget 1024 2`, the same binary as cases 04/06/07. umem_binding=1 (by_dmabuf) is the *configured* transport, asserted against the capture rather than read from it: NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=ibgda with DMABUF left enabled. The other supported configuration (ibdevx + NVSHMEM_IB_DISABLE_DMABUF=1, umem_binding=0) is what SigmaTrace's published artifact uses and is a follow-up case, not a variant of this one — they are different experiments and the param exists so a capture can never again be checked against the wrong one.
oracle_note: The engagement guard runs first and gates everything else. A silent fallback to a CPU-proxy transport produces zero device-initiated traffic, which is indistinguishable from 'the provider captured nothing' — that ambiguity is how case 08's unhooked mlx5dv_create_qp hid behind an empty golden for weeks, and how a probe run earlier this week was read as proving IBGDA engaged when it had failed to initialise entirely.
